.m-dir.why: THE MASCOT'S INNER DOM IS THE `page-mascot` PACKAGE'S, NOT OURS. The design draws the fox from its own markup and we render <Mascot/> from the package, which ships its own structure and styling. Transcribing these would be a second, competing description of a DOM we do not author, and the first time the package changed its internals ours would point at elements that no longer exist. The rendered result is checked by scripts/mascot-check.mjs instead of the rules behind it.

.reserve-aside.why: #654, owner: "this below in the left hand bottom side of the website not in that component". The design draws the reserve notice inside the claim card, where it was the content that pushed the panel past its clamp - 41px hidden at 1280x800 and 128px at 1024x768, concealed rather than shown because .card.claim > .panel scrolls. It is a fact about the faucet's float rather than a step in the claim, and claims keep working while it is up, so it belongs beside the hero copy. Keeps the .phase box so it still reads as one of the page's status panels; only the placement differs from the snapshot.

.reserve-aside .figs-action.why: Owner: the reserve action belongs BESIDE the figures, not stacked under them. Baseline alignment puts the link level with the numbers, and the gap between the figures comes down 1.4u -> .7u to buy width. MEASURED: with the full 'or point a miner' wording the row needed 385/351/356px against 360/319/297px of panel at 1440x900, 1280x800 and 1024x768 - short by 25, 32 and 59px - so the label is the shorter 'or mine' (SDE-App's original call, re-derived here). flex-wrap lets the action drop to its own line rather than force the page sideways on a phone. At .9u the row still stacked at 1024x768 - it needed exactly 297px against 297px of panel - so the gap comes down once more to clear it by a measured margin rather than by a rounding error.

.reserve-aside .reserve-act.why: The same owner ask: right-aligned on the figures' line. margin-left:auto takes the remaining width; nowrap because an action that wraps to two lines defeats putting it on this row at all.

.stage .tag.why:
RE-SCOPED TO OUTRANK globals.css, AND IT ADDS ONE DECLARATION, NAMED. The re-scoping is as above - one ancestor, so it outranks the legacy sheet. What it adds beyond the design's body is:
  text-transform:none
which closes globals.css:151-155 `.tag { ... text-transform: uppercase; ... }`. The legacy sheet upper-cases every tag at the same (0,1,0) specificity as the design's own `.tag`, so source order decided it and the design's tags shipped shouting. #575's review could not see it because `.tag` matched zero elements on that tree - the chips arrive with these views.
Named per the CTO's round-three ruling: an `override` whose body adds to the spec's names each addition and the globals.css rule it closes, or it is a `divergence`. Round three pasted "SAME DECLARATIONS" onto this entry and it was false - the checker's own sameBodies says so.

.stage ::selection.why:
RE-SCOPED TO OUTRANK globals.css, AND IT ADDS ONE DECLARATION, NAMED. The re-scoping is as above - one ancestor, so it outranks the legacy sheet. What it adds beyond the design's body is:
  background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 30%,transparent)

.tabs button.why:
A DEDICATED BORDER TOKEN FOR THE TAB, because the shared one cannot be raised alone. The unselected tab's `--hair` border is #efe6df on #fff: 1.23:1, invisible, so the pair read as a label with grey text rather than two tabs - the owner reported exactly that from a screenshot. WCAG 1.4.11 wants 3.0:1 for a control boundary, and ui-smoke.mjs:1063 argues in this repo's own words that borders are exempt because THE GLYPH identifies the control. That inverts here: the tab is text-only with `background:none`, so its border is the only non-text thing saying 'control'. SDE-UI made that argument on #610 and it is right.

NOT `--prompt-border`, which was my first answer: it is shared with `.prompt`, so raising it to the floor would move the address input's border too. SDE-UI caught that the token question is downstream of the floor question rather than independent.

Values chosen against BOTH backgrounds the tab sits on, not just the page: #968981 is 3.39:1 on --surface and 3.27:1 on --panel; #7d736b is 3.59:1 and 3.41:1 in ink. The obvious candidates one step lighter (#a09289, #736962) clear 3.0 on the surface and FAIL on the panel at 2.91 and 2.95, which is where the card actually is.

.tag.more.why: RE-SCOPED TO OUTRANK globals.css, SAME DECLARATIONS (#575). The legacy sheet styles the same element at the same specificity, so the design's own selector loses on source order alone. One ancestor is added - `html` for element rules, `.stage` for page furniture - which raises specificity without changing what is painted. The spec's key and ours therefore differ while the CSS does not, which the checker reports as one dropped rule plus one added rule: the same divergence twice.

.view.hero .hero-grid.why:
THE FOOTER MUST NEVER MOVE AND THE PAGE MUST NEVER SCROLL, the owner's rule, and this group of rules is what makes it true. The claim card grew with its tallest panel - the sent receipt - past the viewport and pushed the footer below the fold: measured 39px over at 1440x900 and 132px at 1440x720.

THE DESIGN ALREADY INTENDS THIS. Its `.card.claim{max-height:100%}` and `.card.claim > .panel{overflow:auto}` say the card is bounded and its contents scroll inside. Both were inert here because no ancestor had a definite height, so the percentage never resolved. These rules restore the chain the design assumes rather than inventing a mechanism.

WHY IT CAN WORK NOW AND COULD NOT IN S2a. The clamp was removed then because it SWALLOWED content - footer cut by 30-93px, Donate/Terms/GitHub unreachable. The claim card had no inner scroll box; #583 gave it one. The other views still had none, and bounding `.comp` alone broke the status view exactly as before (1081px in a 768px box, all four fit rows red), which is why `.views > .view:not(.hero)` gets its own. Verified after: fit-check 168/168, and four footer links reachable with 0px cut at 1024x768, 1280x720, 1366x768 and 1440x810.

.views > .view.hero, .comp > .view.hero.why: OUR LANDMARK, NOT A #575 RE-SCOPING, and round three mislabelled it. The spec has this as `.comp > .view.hero`. Our four views sit inside a `<main class="views">` landmark rather than directly in `.comp`, so the design's child combinator matched nothing at all and computed padding-top 0. The selector carries BOTH spellings so the rule applies in our structure and still describes the design's. Same declarations as the spec - verified - but the reason is the landmark, and globals.css has nothing to do with it.

.hero-copy.shipped: display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:calc(1.5*var(--u)); align-items:flex-start; align-self:stretch; overflow-y:auto; overscroll-behavior:contain
.hero-copy.why: #687: the column absorbs its own overflow instead of painting it under the footer. Above 56rem the shell is locked to the viewport (.comp 100dvh, .stage overflow hidden) and the hero row is minmax(0,1fr), so this column can be given less height than its content needs. Measured on main at 960x800 with the reserve low: it needs 577px, the row gives 489, and the 88px surplus was painted under the footer - which put the reserve notice's /donate link under the footer's brand image between 940 and 1000px wide at 768 and 800 high, unreachable by click or scroll. The column fits until the reserve-low notice appears (everything else costs 260 of the 457 available) and the notice is 173px, more than compacting could reclaim. Scrolling is what .panel already does one card over - ui-smoke: 'the panel absorbed it by scrolling itself, not by clipping it'. The spec's three declarations are unchanged. align-self:stretch is the one that makes overflow-y mean anything: the grid sets align-items:start, so without it the column is sized to its content and never constrained - measured, scrollHeight and clientHeight were both 577 against a 489px row and the fix changed nothing. A min-height:0 shipped here first and a mutant proved it inert - removing it changed nothing and a 48-viewport re-sweep was clean, because a grid item's automatic minimum size is already zero once overflow is not visible. Dropped rather than kept with a corrected comment.
